pd2-cardiovascular-exam: What is the most common symptom of coronary artery disease?
Chest pain
How should the chest pain history begin?
With open-ended questions, then details
How do patients describe palpitations?
Skipping, racing, fluttering, pounding
How is dyspnea defined?
Awareness of breathing out of proportion to exertion
How is orthopnea quantified?
By the number of pillows used for sleeping
When does paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea typically occur?
One to two hours after going to bed
How is edema defined?
Excess fluid in the extravascular interstitial space
What is the most common cause of syncope?
Neurocardiogenic, also called vasovagal
What is the cardiac cycle?
From the start of one heartbeat to the next
What produces the first heart sound?
Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves
What produces the second heart sound?
Closure of the pulmonic and aortic valves
Which component of S2 is usually louder, and why?
Aortic, reflecting the high pressure in the aorta
When is physiologic splitting of S2 audible?
During inspiration
What is the apical impulse?
The brief impulse of the left ventricular apex
Where is the point of maximal impulse normally found?
Fifth space, at or just medial to midclavicular
What does a hyperkinetic ventricular impulse indicate?
Transiently increased stroke volume
How does the location of the left ventricular impulse differ in volume overload?
Displaced to the left and possibly downward
Where is the right ventricular impulse felt?
The 3rd to 5th left intercostal spaces
Which sounds is the bell better for?
Low-pitched sounds
What is required of stethoscope placement?
Direct contact with the patient's skin
Which lighting is specified for the cardiovascular examination?
Tangential lighting
Where and how is S1 best heard, and what is its relation to the carotid pulse?
Diaphragm at the apex, before the carotid pulse
Where is normal physiologic splitting of S2 best heard?
The pulmonic area
When do early systolic ejection sounds occur, and what do they indicate?
Shortly after S1; they indicate disease
What usually causes a systolic click?
Mitral valve prolapse
When does S3 occur, and how is it best heard?
Early in diastole, with the bell at the apex
When does S4 occur, and what is its cadence?
Just before S1, cadence Ten-nes-SEE
What causes an opening snap?
Abrupt deceleration as a stenotic mitral valve opens
What produces a murmur?
Turbulent blood flow over a valve
How is a thrill assessed?
With the balls of the hand against the chest wall
Which seven characteristics describe a murmur?
Timing, shape, location, radiation, intensity
How can palpating the carotid help with murmur timing?
Systolic murmurs match the carotid upstroke
What defines the shape of a murmur?
Its intensity over time
How is murmur intensity graded?
A six-point scale, written as a fraction
Which words describe the quality of a murmur?
Blowing, harsh, rumbling, musical
What does the radiation of a murmur help establish?
Site of origin, intensity, flow direction
